name: v2_default
_comment_models: Benchmark v2 roster: every model that runs on the v2-only targets (see cluster/submit_v2_sweep.py). TABDPT is not in v2; TABDPT-V1.3 (the tabarena TabDPT v1.3 wrapper) is. NOT_RUN in submit_v2_sweep.py (CHAKRA-TAB, CHAKRA-TAB-FULL, TABSTAR, AUTOGLUON-EXTREME-4H) stay out of the sweep. Onboarding and removal history is in the git log of this file and in CHANGELOG.md.
_comment_compute_scaling: num_bag_folds (was 8) and time_limit (was 3600) both cut 2026-09-25 as a deliberate compute-scaling decision, alongside target_list.json's n_repeats=1 (see configs/v1/README.md). Impact differs by model class: compute-bound models (LIMIX/TABICL/TABFM/TabPFN-family -- finish well under their old time budget regardless of fold count) get a roughly proportional ~(3/8) compute cut per task with no real quality risk. Time-budget-bound models (MITRA is the confirmed case: consistently used ~59 of its 60 allotted minutes every fold, never early-stopping) are a real risk here -- AutoGluon's fold time-budgeting (time_limit_fold = (time_left/folds_left)*0.8) means the full 600s is now split across only 3 folds instead of 8, so MITRA-class fine-tuning gets meaningfully fewer training epochs per fold than before, likely undertrained relative to its earlier (still not fully converged) runs. Not fixed here -- flagged so a future review of MITRA/RAMANFORMER/REALMLP/TABM-class results interprets a score drop correctly (compute starvation, not necessarily a worse architecture). model_time_limit_overrides below are unaffected (they're already-calibrated absolute floors well above 600s for specific slow/wide (model, dataset) pairs) and stay in force.
_comment_max_train_samples_overrides: Global (every model, both SLURM and k8s backends -- see cluster/submit_job.py's resolve_max_train_samples), unlike model_time_limit_overrides which is model-specific. Added 2026-09-25 after REZERONET's real TimeLimitExceeded on mlrod (130,061 rows) under the 600s/3-bag-fold compute-scaling settings: 90/93 large-pod tasks succeeded with real, confirmed GPU utilization (the GPU-tier resource-declaration fix, see bridge_bases._GPURequiredBridge), only mlrod's 3 tasks (repeat=0, folds 0-2) failed on time budget. 10000 is a deliberate row cap (~13x fewer rows than mlrod's 130061) chosen to fit comfortably in the 600s/3-fold budget while keeping a substantial training set -- not recalibrated against a real measured runtime the way time_limit_overrides' 10800 was, so revisit if a model still times out at this cap. EXTENDED 2026-09-26: the same TimeLimitExceeded pattern was confirmed live for the other two row-count outliers in 'large_datasets' -- wheat_lines (53,134 rows) and bacteria_identification (78,500 rows) -- across multiple GPU-tier models (COATNET, SANET, ROCKET, TABICLV2) once they were actually training on GPU. Applied the same flat 10000 cap for consistency rather than scaling proportionally to each dataset's row count; revisit per-dataset if 10000 still isn't enough headroom for a given model.
_comment_model_max_train_samples_overrid: Per-model row cap (cluster/submit_job.py's resolve_max_train_samples), applied on top of max_train_samples_overrides above -- the smaller of the two wins. Added 2026-09-26 after PERPETUAL_BOOSTER's real OOMKilled crash on wheat_lines: already capped to 10000 rows by the global override above, only 1738 features/44MB, yet OOMKilled a 256GB pod within ~27s -- points to a per-fit memory blowup in the 'perpetual' library itself, not anything that actually scales with row count, so this is a cheap-to-try mitigation, not a confirmed fix; watch whether PERPETUAL_BOOSTER still OOMs at this lower cap. Flat int (not dataset-keyed) -- applies to EVERY dataset for this model, not just mlrod/wheat_lines/bacteria_identification. EXTENDED 2026-09-26 (same day): MITRA, TABFM, REALTABPFN-V2, and REALTABPFN-V2.5 all confirmed TimeLimitExceeded on wheat_lines/mlrod even at the 10000-row global cap -- unlike PERPETUAL_BOOSTER, these ARE genuinely row-count-driven (foundation/transformer models whose per-fit cost scales with training-set size), so a lower cap should directly help. TABICL's NotEnoughCudaMemoryError is the same underlying driver from a different angle: it's an in-context transformer whose GPU memory footprint scales with the number of training rows held in context. 5000 is a deliberate, not-calibrated halving of the existing 10000 cap for all five -- revisit per-model if 5000 still isn't enough headroom. MITRA LOWERED 5000->3000 (2026-09-28): confirmed live that MITRA-large's entire remaining gap (wheat_lines, mlrod, bacteria_identification, sugar_mixtures_low_snr) still failed at the 5000-row cap -- MITRA is documented elsewhere in this file as strictly time-budget-bound (never early-stops, uses ~all of its allotted time every fold), so a further row cut directly buys back training time rather than risking a memory regression. TA-MITRA-V2 ADDED 3000 (2026-09-29): confirmed real CUDA memory-fragmentation OOM warnings (expandable_segments mapping failures against a near-fully-consumed device) on MITRA-full and TA-MITRA-V2-full's A100 pods; unlike MITRA, TA-MITRA-V2 previously had no row cap at all despite being the same fine-tuning-based architecture family with the identical symptom -- added the same 3000 cap for consistency. Paired with lowering TA-MITRA-V2's own max_features_budget (see ta_mitra_v2/hpo.py's manual_configs) since Mitra-v2 has a real, tunable column-reduction mechanism MITRA (v1) lacks. LIMIX 5000 (2026-10-03): real torch.OutOfMemoryError on an 80GB A100 on wheat_lines (6666x1748 after the 10000-row dataset cap; tried to allocate 18.7GB with 66GB already in use) -- same 5000 as TABICL/TABFM/REALTABPFN-V2. Affects mlrod, bacteria_identification, wheat_lines, serum_prostate_cancer, sugar_mixtures_low_snr, bioprocess_substrates, rruff_mineral_raw; LIMIX results on those were recomputed under the cap. mlrod lowered further to 2000: still a real CUDA OOM at 5000 (16 classes, 3333x1836 train; tried to allocate 23.9 GiB with ~73 GB in use on an 80 GB A100). ORIONMSP {mlrod, wheat_lines: 4000} (2026-10-03): its only never-completed targets were clean skips by VRAM_CAPPED_MODELS' calibrated attention-buffer predicate (40 GiB budget) at the 10000-row dataset cap (~6667 train rows: 61.6/67.8 GiB predicted). 4000 rows -> 30.8/33.9 GiB, under budget. Per-dataset, not model-wide, so ORIONMSP's existing results on its other large datasets (rruff, bacteria_identification, serum_prostate_cancer) stay valid. ORIONMSP lowered to 2000 (2026-10-03): at 4000 rows both datasets CUDA-OOM on an 80 GB A100 (wheat_lines ~106 GB, mlrod ~79 GB peak). CAUSILO ADDED 2026-10-05 (5000): TimeLimitExceeded on mlrod at the 10000-row global cap even on a GPU pod (BHT, 600s/3 bag folds), the same row-count-driven pattern as the foundation models above; same 5000 cap.
_comment_large_datasets: k8s-only (submit_full_benchmark.py's k8s branch): routed to a separate single pod on a bigger GPU (H100/H200) instead of the main A100 pod, so the main sweep isn't dominated by these outliers. Two disjoint kinds of 'large', both real: the top 6 by row count (mlrod 130061, bacteria_identification 78500, wheat_lines 53134, serum_prostate_cancer 12601, sugar_mixtures_low_snr 7840, bioprocess_substrates 6960 -- clear cliff after these, next is 12601 already listed then a drop to 4020) stress GPU batch-size/training memory; the 9 extremely wide ones (~11084-11689 features, 14-235 rows: acetic_acid_species, citric_acid_species, flow_microgel_synthesis, formic_acid_species, itaconic_acid_species, levulinic_acid_species, microgel_size_raw_global, microgel_synthesis, succinic_acid_species) stress feature-dimension memory instead (PCA/GCU representation size, TabPFN's per-forward-pass feature cap) -- unrelated mechanism, just also 'large' in a different axis. 6 more equally-wide microgel_size_*_global variants exist in data/precomputed/dataset_stats.json but aren't in target_list.json (not part of the routine sweep), so they're excluded here too. bioprocess_analytes_kaiser ADDED 2026-09-29: confirmed real TABICL NotEnoughCudaMemoryError on the main A100 pod (all 9 tasks: 3 targets x 3 folds) -- only 134 rows but 5472 features, well below the ~11084+ threshold of the 'extremely wide' cluster above but still wide enough to OOM TabICL specifically; not previously flagged because no model had hit this ceiling on it before. Confirms the wide-dataset OOM risk is a continuum, not a fixed feature-count cutoff -- revisit the other not-yet-flagged wide-ish datasets if another model hits the same error on one.
_comment_model_time_limit_overrides: EBM's real TimeLimitExceeded on wide datasets was mostly interpret's own O(n_features^2) interaction-ranking pre-scan (see Prep_EBM._fit's docstring) -- fixed at the model level (interactions=0 above 4000 features), not by budget alone. A real calibration run post-fix (microgel_synthesis, 11084 features, run_experiment.py --model EBM --time-limit 900 --num-bag-folds 8; this measurement predates the 2026-09-25 removal of small-dataset bag-fold auto-scaling, so it ran at 2 effective folds for this 14-row dataset -- num_bag_folds no longer scales down for any dataset size now, so a rerun would use the routine 3-fold (or whatever --num-bag-folds is passed) instead) finished in 426s wall time (400s training) at 2 folds, already well inside the 3600s default. These 5400s entries are headroom, not a required fix: the other 9 targets in the same 11084-11689-feature cluster have more rows and so used the full 8 bag folds at calibration time (now always whatever --num-bag-folds is configured, currently 3), extrapolating to roughly 4x -> ~1700s -- 5400s leaves ample margin over that for a slower cluster CPU than the one calibrated on, and only more so now that folds never scale below the configured value. ORIONMSP's pharmaceutical_ingredients entry is similarly a safety margin, not the primary fix -- see cluster/profiles/htw.yaml's ORIONMSP mem_tier: a real local run there (2 bag folds) finished fitting in ~175s but then crashed from memory (~25-27GB RSS on a 36GB machine), i.e. this dataset's real confirmed risk is memory, not time. LR's entry is a bare number (not a dataset-keyed dict) -- a blanket override applied regardless of dataset (see cluster/submit_job.py::resolve_time_limit's scalar-override handling). Confirmed real: LR's bagged fold fit on wheat_lines/bacteria_identification takes ~530-560s/fold x 8 sequential folds (~4240-4480s), past the 3600s default, so AutoGluon's fold-fitting strategy extrapolated from an early fold and aborted with TimeLimitExceeded before the (finite, just slower-than-guessed) remaining folds got a chance -- same failure mode already seen for PLS on mlrod, just not yet hit for LR until these two datasets. Under the routine config_index=0 backlog (no HPO search opted in), a time cap on a model like LR doesn't bound anything meaningful -- it only risks this same early-abort happening again on some other not-yet-encountered (model, dataset) pair. 800000s (~9.3 days) is comfortably under the real backstop, the SLURM array's own --time (the profile's default_time, 10 days) -- independent of this value. PERPETUAL_BOOSTER entries (2026-10-03) are a real, observed fix, not headroom: on HTW (refreshed env, routine 600s/3-bag-fold settings, rows already capped at 3000 via model_max_train_samples_overrides) every fold of wheat_lines and serum_alzheimer_disease raised TimeLimitExceeded at 600s (peak RSS 86GB of 256GB, so not memory) -- these 7 datasets are exactly its 7 never-completed classification targets. 5400s matches EBM's budget above. LIMIX (2026-10-03, fresh GPU sweep on HTW A100-80GB): model-wide 800000 (same 'no meaningful cap' convention as LR), not per-dataset -- 3600 was tried first and still hit TimeLimitExceeded on bacteria_identification (30 classes: ~2050s for ONE bag-fold's evaluation, so ~6300s for 3 folds). Originally: -- LimiX is pure in-context inference (no training loop), so a bigger budget changes only whether a task finishes, never its predictions; at 600s it raised TimeLimitExceeded after one bag-fold's OOF evaluation took 193s on locust_phase_hemolymph (3325x855). TABFM (2026-10-03): its 5 >10-class datasets (exactly its never-completed targets) go through tabpfn_extensions' ManyClassClassifier output coding around the 10-class head -- one bag-fold's OOF evaluation alone took 493s on cancer_cell_cooh (12 classes, 422x2090) on an 80GB A100, so 3 folds can't fit in 600s; rruff (79) / bacteria (30) need far more codes. Inference-only model, so the larger budget changes completion, not predictions. REALTABPFN-V2.6 (2026-10-03): same many-class output-coding cost as TABFM once its max_classes cap was lifted (see wrapped_models.py) -- one bag-fold's evaluation took 314s on bacteria_identification (30 classes, 6666x1000) -> TimeLimitExceeded at 600s. cancer_cell_* (12 classes) already fit in 600s, so only the 3 largest many-class datasets. REALTABPFN-V2 (2026-10-03): same many-class output-coding cost on bacteria_identification (30 classes, capped to 5000 rows) -- 201s for one bag-fold's evaluation -> TimeLimitExceeded at 600s; its only never-completed target besides mlrod, which already completes under mlrod's 10800s dataset-level budget. RAMANTRANSFORMER (2026-10-03): only its TimeLimitExceeded datasets (17 tasks on HTW, never completed anywhere) -- its other 119 HTW failures are the documented NaN-validation-loss collapse (80) and CUDA OOM on the ~11k-feature acid-species/microgel targets (39), both genuine model limitations left as documented failures, not budget issues. Outcome: the longer budget lets these finish, but 7 of the first 10 completed reruns collapsed to near-constant predictions (accuracy = majority class, R2 ~0) -- the same instability, surfacing as collapse instead of NaN; kept as genuine results. MITRA/TA-MITRA-V2 (2026-10-03): same 5 >10-class datasets as TABFM, now fit through RamanBench's eager ECOC wrapper (preprocessing/many_class_mitra.py) -- one fine-tuned Mitra per codebook row (up to ~9), so the routine 600s can't cover 3 bag folds. Previously these 30 tasks crashed outright (fixed 10-class head). ORIONMSP (2026-10-03): mlrod/wheat_lines even at the 4000-row cap exceed 600s (TimeLimitExceeded before the first bag fold). MITRA raised to 10800 after the cancer_cell_cooh smoke test took 6630s of its 7200s (v1 fine-tunes ~2x slower than TA-MITRA-V2's 3460s). LIMIX2 (2026-10-03): same model-wide 800000 as LIMIX (inference-only, so the budget changes completion, not predictions) -- at 3600s, 25 of the first 28 large-dataset tasks on BHT raised TimeLimitExceeded (bioprocess_substrates, bacteria_identification, mlrod, serum_prostate_cancer). CAUSILO's large_datasets entries (2026-10-05): a single forward-pass foundation model whose fit does not use extra time to improve (unlike time-budgeted boosters/fine-tuners), so a longer limit only prevents aborts and gives it no advantage; it hit TimeLimitExceeded on mlrod at 600s even at its 5000-row cap. HIVECOTEV2 (2026-10-06): model-wide 21600s by the maintainers' decision, a deliberate departure from the protocol's 600s, not a fix for an observed failure. aeon's HIVECOTEV2 turns the fit's time limit into its own time contract (each component gets a sixth of it), so at 600s (~200s per bag fold) it would run as a heavily truncated HC2. Its four components (STC, DRCIF, ARSENAL, TDE) run on the protocol's normal budget and are assembled into HC2 offline (scripts/assemble_hivecote.py), so both a budget-matched and a long-budget HC2 are reported. TABSTAR (2026-10-05, 3600): back in the sweep with the original pre-2026-09-25 budget. At 600s it ran ~9-10 epochs (~58s each on larger datasets) and was always cut off before its own early stopping (patience 5, tabstar.training.hyperparams.FINETUNE_PATIENCE); all three 600s results used ~560-590s and were far off the field (e.g. ROC AUC ~0.6 on comfile_stroke). TabArena gives every config 3600s, so this is TabArena's own budget, not extra headroom; it does mean TABSTAR gets more time than time-budget-bound models still on 600s (MITRA, see _comment_compute_scaling).
_comment_v2: Benchmark v2 (branch v2, RELEASING.md 'Branches'): every v1 target plus the v2-only targets (target_list.json field since='v2'), with min_groups_per_class=3. Models, time limits and caps as v1. glioma_idh, raman_mpi and stroke_urine_sers_* (above the 10,000-row cap) get the overrides wheat_lines has.
